description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/lib.rs:62, 65

```rust
pub use jmap_sharing_types::JMAP_PRINCIPALS_URI;
pub use jmap_sharing_types::JMAP_PRINCIPALS_OWNER_URI;
```

Two problems:

1. **Dual public location.** Both `jmap_sharing_types::JMAP_PRINCIPALS_URI`
   and `jmap_sharing_server::JMAP_PRINCIPALS_URI` resolve to the same
   `&'static str`. Documentation, examples, and downstream code paths
   diverge — half of them will use the types-crate path, half the
   server-crate path. Refactoring later (e.g. moving the constant into
   a sub-module of the types crate) breaks the re-export silently.

2. **Diverges from canonical mail-server.** `jmap-mail-server`
   declares its URI constants locally:

   ```rust
   // crate-jmap-mail-server/src/lib.rs:45
   pub const JMAP_MAIL_URI: &str = \"urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail\";
   pub const JMAP_SUBMISSION_URI: &str = \"urn:ietf:params:jmap:submission\";
   pub const JMAP_VACATION_RESPONSE_URI: &str = \"urn:ietf:params:jmap:vacationresponse\";
   ```

   `jmap-mail-types` does NOT declare these — grep confirms zero
   occurrences in `crate-jmap-mail-types/src/`. So the canonical pattern
   is \"server crate is the single public home for URI strings\".

   `jmap-sharing-types` does declare both URIs (`capability.rs:15` etc.).
   The proper canonical-template alignment is one of:
   - Move declarations to `jmap-sharing-server` and have
     `jmap-sharing-types` re-export them (or remove the types-crate
     declaration if no consumer needs it there).
   - Move canonical mail's `JMAP_*_URI` declarations into
     `jmap-mail-types` and re-export from `jmap-mail-server`, then
     propagate to all siblings.

   Either direction is fine; the current state where two siblings have
   genuinely-different homes for the same kind of constant is wrong.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: a contributor cuts
and pastes a `use jmap_X_server::JMAP_X_URI;` example from one crate to
another, hits a compile error in some siblings, and learns the hard way
that the workspace's URI constants live in two homes depending on which
sibling they are talking to. Real productivity tax.

Note: this finding is partially out-of-scope (it touches both the types
and server crate boundaries), but the public-API expansion lives in the
server crate's diff. Mention here so the resolution bead can decide
which direction to consolidate.
title: JMAP_PRINCIPALS_URI / JMAP_PRINCIPALS_OWNER_URI re-exports create dual public locations; diverges from canonical mail-server's local declaration
